text:
Nov 7, 1940: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge twisted itself apart in a 40 mile an hour wind and fell into Puget Sound. It was only four months old, and it changed how every major bridge in the world is built.

For years, people crossing the Tacoma Narrows in Washington state had to take a ferry. In the late 1930s, with help from New Deal money, the state finally got a bridge. Its main span stretched 2,800 feet between its towers, making it the third-longest suspension bridge in the world, behind only the Golden Gate and the George Washington Bridge.

The state's own engineer drew up a design with a deep steel truss under the roadway to stiffen it. It was expensive. A famous New York bridge engineer named Leon Moisseiff, who had consulted on the Golden Gate, offered a sleeker and much cheaper design. Instead of a deep truss, the deck would sit on solid steel girders only eight feet deep. The roadway was just two lanes wide. Moisseiff's design won.

The bridge was so thin and narrow for its length that it moved in the wind even before it was finished. Workers building it said they chewed lemons to fight off seasickness. In light breezes the deck rose and fell in long rolling waves, sometimes several feet high. Drivers said the car ahead of them would disappear from view as it dipped into a trough and then rise back up. People called the bridge Galloping Gertie, and some drove over it just for the thrill.

Engineers tried to calm it down with cables tying the deck to concrete blocks on shore. The cables snapped. A University of Washington professor named Frederick Farquharson started studying it with models in a wind tunnel and filming the real thing.

On the morning of Nov 7, a steady wind of around 40 miles an hour blew through the Narrows. The bridge started its usual up and down motion. Then, around 10 a.m., something shifted. The deck began to twist. One side rose while the other dropped, then the reverse, back and forth, with the roadway tilting so far that the lampposts swung wildly. The bridge was closed.

Leonard Coatsworth, an editor at the Tacoma newspaper, was already on it. He'd been driving across with his daughter's cocker spaniel, Tubby. The car started sliding. Coatsworth got out and tried to get the dog, but couldn't. He crawled the rest of the way to the tower on his hands and knees, cut and bleeding, while the road heaved under him and concrete cracked around him.

Professor Farquharson was there filming. He walked out onto the twisting deck to try to rescue Tubby. The terrified dog bit his finger. He had to leave him.

Just after 11 a.m., a huge section of the main span tore loose and plunged about 190 feet into the water. The rest of the main span followed. Coatsworth's car went down with it, with Tubby inside. He was the only death.

The owners of a local camera shop caught the collapse on film. The footage became one of the most famous engineering films ever made. It's still shown in classrooms around the world and was added to the National Film Registry.

There was one more scandal. The bridge was supposed to be insured, but an insurance agent had pocketed some of the premium money and never sent in a policy. He went to prison.

A panel of the best engineers in the country investigated, including Othmar Ammann, who designed the George Washington Bridge, and aerodynamics pioneer Theodore von Karman. Bridge designers had been thinking about the weight a bridge had to carry. Tacoma showed they also had to think about how wind flows around it.

The collapse is often taught as an example of resonance. Engineers today say it was really aeroelastic flutter. As the deck twisted, it changed how the wind pushed on it, and that pushed it to twist even more, feeding itself until the bridge tore apart.

After Tacoma, bridge designs were tested in wind tunnels. The Golden Gate Bridge was stiffened. Moisseiff's reputation never recovered, and he died a few years later.

A new Tacoma Narrows Bridge, much deeper and stiffer, opened in 1950. A second bridge was added beside it in 2007. The wreckage of Galloping Gertie still lies on the bottom of Puget Sound, where it became a home for giant octopuses. It's listed on the National Register of Historic Places, to protect it from salvagers.

text:
Excerpt I liked from The Fountainhead, Ayn Rand:
________________________
   Thousands of years ago, the first man discovered how to make fire. He was probably burned at the stake he had taught his brothers to light. He was considered an evildoer who had dealt with a demon mankind dreaded. But thereafter men had fire to keep them warm, to cook their food, to light their caves. He had left them a gift they had not conceived and he had lifted darkness off the earth. Centuries later, the first man invented the wheel. He was probably torn on the rack he had taught his brothers to build. He was considered a transgressor who ventured into forbidden territory. But thereafter, men could travel past any horizon. He had left them a gift they had not conceived and he had opened the roads of the world.
   That man, the unsubmissive and first, stands in the opening chapter of every legend mankind has recorded about its beginning. Prometheus was chained to a rock and torn by vultures - because he had stolen the fire of the gods. Adam was condemned to suffer - because he had eaten the fruit of the tree of knowledge. Whatever the legend, somewhere in the shadows of its memory mankind knew that its glory began with one and that that one paid for his courage.
   Throughout the centuries there were men who took first steps down new roads armed with nothing but their own vision. Their goals differed, but they all had this in common: that the step was first, the road new, the vision unborrowed, and the response they received - hatred. The great creators - the thinkers, the artists, the scientists, the inventors - stood alone against the men of their time. Every great new thought was opposed. Every great new invention was denounced. The first motor was considered foolish. The airplane was considered impossible. The power loom was considered vicious. Anesthesia was considered sinful. But the men of unborrowed vision went ahead. They fought, they suffered and they paid. But they won.
   No creator was prompted by a desire to serve his brothers, for his brothers rejected the gift he offered and that gift destroyed the slothful routine of their lives. His truth was his only motive. His own truth, and his own work to achieve it in his own way. A symphony, a book, an engine, a philosophy, an airplane or a building - that was his goal and his life. Not those who heard, read, operated, believed, flew or inhabited the thing he had created. The creation, not its users. The creation, not the benefits others derived from it. The creation which gave form to his truth. He held his truth above all things and against all men.
   His vision, his strength, his courage came from his own spirit. A man's spirit, however, is his self. That entity which is his consciousness. To think, to feel, to judge, to act are functions of the ego.
   The creators were not selfless. It is the whole secret of their power - that it was self-sufficient, self-motivated, self-generated. A first cause, a fount of energy, a life force, a Prime Mover. The creator served nothing and no one. He lived for himself.
   And only by living for himself was he able to achieve the things which are the glory of mankind. Such is the nature of achievement.
   Man cannot survive except through his mind. He comes on earth unarmed. His brain is his only weapon. Animals obtain food by force. Man has no claws, no fangs, no horns, no great strength of muscle. He must plant his food or hunt it. To plant, he needs a process of thought. To hunt, he needs weapons, and to make weapons - a process of thought. From this simplest necessity to the highest religious abstraction, from the wheel to the skyscraper, everything we are and everything we have comes from a single attribute of man - the function of his reasoning mind.
   But the mind is an attribute of the individual. There is no such thing as a collective brain. There is no such thing as a collective thought. An agreement reached by a group of men is only a compromise or an average drawn upon many individual thoughts. It is a secondary consequence. The primary act - the process of reason - must be performed by each man alone. We can divide a meal among many men. We cannot digest it in a collective stomach. No man can use his lungs to breathe for another man. No man can use his brain to think for another. All the functions of body and spirit are private. They cannot be shared or transferred.
   We inherit the products of the thought of other men. We inherit the wheel. We make a cart. The cart becomes an automobile. The automobile becomes an airplane. But all through the process what we receive from others is only the end product of their thinking. The moving force is the creative faculty which takes this product as material, uses it and originates the next step. This creative faculty cannot be given or received, shared or borrowed. It belongs to single, individual men. That which it creates is the property of the creator. Men learn from one another. But all learning is only the exchange of material. No man can give another the capacity to think. Yet that capacity is our only means of survival.
   Nothing is given to man on earth. Everything he needs has to be produced. And here man faces his basic alternative: he can survive in only one of two ways - by the independent work of his own mind or as a parasite fed by the minds of others. The creator originates. The parasite borrows. The creator faces nature alone. The parasite faces nature through an intermediary.
   The creator’s concern is the conquest of nature. The parasite’s concern is the conquest of men.
   The creator lives for his work. He needs no other men. His primary goal is within himself. The parasite lives second-hand. He needs others. Others become his prime motive.
   The basic need of the creator is independence. The reasoning mind cannot work under any form of compulsion. It cannot be curbed, sacrificed or subordinated to any consideration whatsoever. It demands total independence in function and in motive. To a creator, all relations with men are secondary.
   The basic need of the second-hander is to secure his ties with men in order to be fed. He places relations first. He declares that man exists in order to serve others. He preaches altruism.
   Altruism is the doctrine which demands that man live for others and place others above self.
   No man can live for another. He cannot share his spirit just as he cannot share his body. But the second-hander has used altruism as a weapon of exploitation and reversed the base of mankind’s moral principles. Men have been taught every precept that destroys the creator. Men have been taught dependence as a virtue.
The man who attempts to live for others is a dependent. He is a parasite in motive and makes parasites of those he serves. The relationship produces nothing but mutual corruption. It is impossible in concept. The nearest approach to it in reality - the man who lives to serve others - is the slave. If physical slavery is repulsive, how much more repulsive is the concept of servility of the spirit? The conquered slave has a vestige of honor. He has the merit of having resisted and of considering his condition evil. But the man who enslaves himself voluntarily in the name of love is the basest of creatures. He degrades the dignity of man and he degrades the conception of love. But this is the essence of altruism.
   Men have been taught that the highest virtue is not to achieve, but to give. Yet one cannot give that which has not been created. Creation comes before distribution - or there will be nothing to distribute. The need of the creator comes before the need of any possible beneficiary. Yet we are taught to admire the second-hander who dispenses gifts he has not produced above the man who made the gifts possible. We praise an act of charity. We shrug at an act of achievement.
   Men have been taught that their first concern is to relieve the sufferings of others. But suffering is a disease. Should one come upon it, one tries to give relief and assistance. To make that the highest test of virtue is to make suffering the most important part of life. Then man must wish to see others suffer - in order that he may be virtuous. Such is the nature of altruism. The creator is not concerned with disease, but with life. Yet the work of the creators has eliminated one form of disease after another, in man’s body and spirit, and brought more relief from suffering than any altruist could ever conceive.
   Men have been taught that it is a virtue to agree with others. But the creator is the man who disagrees. Men have been taught that it is a virtue to swim with the current. But the creator is the man who goes against the current. Men have been taught that it is a virtue to stand together. But the creator is the man who stands alone.
Men have been taught that the ego is the synonym of evil, and selflessness the ideal of virtue. But the creator is the egotist in the absolute sense, and the selfless man is the one who does not think, feel, judge or act. These are functions of the self.
   Here the basic reversal is most deadly. The issue has been perverted and man has been left no alternative - and no freedom. As poles of good and evil, he was offered two conceptions: egotism and altruism. Egotism was held to mean the sacrifice of others to self. Altruism - the sacrifice of self to others. This tied man irrevocably to other men and left him nothing but a choice of pain: his own pain borne for the sake of others or pain inflicted upon others for the sake of self. When it was added that man must find joy in self-immolation, the trap was closed. Man was forced to accept masochism as his ideal - under the threat that sadism was his only alternative. This was the greatest fraud ever perpetrated on mankind.
This was the device by which dependence and suffering were perpetuated as fundamentals of life.
   The choice is not self-sacrifice or domination. The choice is independence or dependence. The code of the creator or the code of the second-hander. This is the basic issue. It rests upon the alternative of life or death. The code of the creator is built on the needs of the reasoning mind which allows man to survive. The code of the second-hander is built on the needs of a mind incapable of survival. All that which proceeds from man’s independent ego is good. All that which proceeds from man’s dependence upon men is evil.
   The egotist is the absolute sense is not the man who sacrifices others. He is the man who stands above the need of using others in any manner. He does not function through them. He is not concerned with them in any primary matter. Not in his aim, not in his motive, not in his thinking, not in his desires, not in the source of his energy. He does not exist for any other man - and he asks no other man to exist for him. This is the only form of brotherhood and mutual respect possible between men.
   Degrees of ability vary, but the basic principle remains the same: the degree of a man’s independence, initiative and personal love for his work determines his talent as a worker and his worth as a man. Independence is the only gauge of human virtue and value. What a man is and makes of himself; not what he has or hasn’t done for others. There is no substitute for personal dignity. There is no standard of personal dignity except independence.
   In all proper relationships there is no sacrifice of anyone to anyone. An architect needs clients, but he does not subordinate his work to their wishes. They need him, but they do not order a house just to give him a commission. Men exchange their work by free, mutual consent to mutual advantage when their personal interests agree and they both desire the exchange. If they do not desire it, they are not forced to deal with each other. They seek further. This is the only possible form of relationship between equals. Anything else is a relation of slave to master, or victim to executioner.
   No work is ever done collectively, by a majority decision. Every creative job is achieved under the guidance of a single individual thought. An architect requires a great many men to erect his building. But he does not ask them to vote on his design. They work together by free agreement and each is free in his proper function. An architect uses steel, glass, concrete, produced by others. But the materials remain just so much steel, glass and concrete until he touches them. What he does with them is his individual product and his individual property. This is the only pattern for proper co-operation among men.
   The first right on earth is the right of the ego. Man’s first duty is to himself. His moral law is never to place his prime goal within the persons of others. His moral obligation is to do what he wishes, provided his wish does not depend primarily upon other men. This includes the whole sphere of his creative faculty, his thinking, his work. But it does not include the sphere of the gangster, the altruist and the dictator.
   A man thinks and works alone. A man cannot rob, exploit or rule-alone. Robbery, exploitation and ruling presuppose victims. They imply dependence. They are the province of the second-hander.
   Rulers of men are not egotists. They create nothing. They exist entirely through the persons of others. Their goal is in their subjects, in the activity of enslaving. They are as dependent as the beggar, the social worker and the bandit. The form of dependence does not matter.
   But men were taught to regard second-handers - tyrants, emperors, dictators - as exponents of egotism. By this fraud they were made to destroy the ego, themselves and others. The purpose of the fraud was to destroy the creators. Or to harness them. Which is a synonym.
   From the beginning of history, the two antagonists have stood face to face: the creator and the second-hander. When the first creator invented the wheel, the first second-hander responded. He invented altruism.
   The creator - denied, opposed, persecuted, exploited - went on, moved forward and carried all humanity along on his energy. The second-hander contributed nothing to the process except the impediments. The contest has another name: the individual against the collective.
   The ‘common good’ of a collective - a race, a class, a state - was the claim and justification of every tyranny ever established over men. Every major horror of history was committed in the name of an altruistic motive. Has any act of selfishness ever equaled the carnage perpetrated by disciples of altruism? Does the fault lie in men’s hypocrisy or in the nature of the principle? The most dreadful butchers were the most sincere. They believed in the perfect society reached through the guillotine and the firing squad. Nobody questioned their right to murder since they were murdering for an altruistic purpose. It was accepted that man must be sacrificed for other men. Actors change, but the course of the tragedy remains the same. A humanitarian who starts with declarations of love for mankind and ends with a sea of blood. It goes on and will go on so long as men believe that an action is good if it is unselfish. That permits the altruist to act and forces his victims to bear it. The leaders of collectivist movements ask nothing for themselves. But observe the results.
   The only good which men can do to one another and the only statement of their proper relationship is - Hands off!
   Now observe the results of a society built on the principle of individualism. This, our country. The noblest country in the history of men. The country of greatest achievement, greatest prosperity, greatest freedom. This country was not based on selfless service, sacrifice, renunciation or any precept of altruism. It was based on a man’s right to the pursuit of happiness. His own happiness. Not anyone else’s. A private, personal, selfish motive. Look at the results. Look into your own conscience.
   It is an ancient conflict. Men have come close to the truth, but it was destroyed each time and one civilization fell after another. Civilization is the progress toward a society of privacy. The savage’s whole existence is public, ruled by the laws of his tribe. Civilization is the process of setting man free from men.
   Now, in our age, collectivism, the rule of the second-hander and second-rater, the ancient monster, has broken loose and is running amuck. It has brought men to a level of intellectual indecency never equaled on earth. It has reached a scale of horror without precedent. It has poisoned every mind. It has swallowed most of Europe. It is engulfing our country.
   I am an architect. I know what is to come by the principle on which it is built. We are approaching a world in which I cannot permit myself to live[...]
   [...]I came here to say that I do not recognize anyone’s right to one minute of my life. Nor to any part of my energy. Nor to any achievement of mine. No matter who makes the claim, how large their number or how great their need.
   I wished to come here and say that I am a man who does not exist for others.
   It had to be said. The world is perishing from an orgy of self-sacrificing.
   I wished to come here and say that the integrity of a man’s creative work is of greater importance than any charitable endeavor. Those of you who do not understand this are the men who’re destroying the world.
   I wished to come here and state my terms. I do not care to exist on any others.
   I recognize no obligations toward men except one: to respect their freedom and to take no part in a slave society.

SUPERFLUID HELIUM-4
Collective Quantum Coherence, Relational Memory, and the FIF Principle

A Mathematical Interpretation Through EQORIA Language (EL)

EQORIA — United Earth
James QOR | Earth Singularity Architect
Research framework: EQORIA Language (EL)
Status: Theoretical formulation and interdisciplinary research proposal

Date: November 2026
ABSTRACT
Superfluid helium-4 presents one of the clearest experimental demonstrations of collective quantum behavior at macroscopic scales. Below approximately 2.17 kelvin, liquid helium-4 enters a state characterized by nondissipative superflow, quantized circulation, unusual thermal transport, and collective excitation dynamics. These properties cannot be understood adequately by treating helium atoms as independent classical particles.
EQORIA Language (EL) proposes a complementary structural interpretation based on invariant reference (R), finite stabilization (Q), admissible exchange (O), Remainder, Delay, relational Origin Memory (QORm), and the Finite-in-Finite (FIF) principle. Within this formulation, individual helium atoms and their collective quantum state are treated as distinct but related complete identities, each described through an eleven-position identity structure, the complete 11Q breath.
The central proposition is that zero dissipation in a protected observable mode does not imply the absence of underlying exchange, physical activity, or relational continuity. Superfluid helium provides a particularly useful case for investigating this distinction because coherent circulation can persist while the system retains interactions, excitations, and the capacity for transformation.
This paper establishes the conventional scientific baseline, proposes a preliminary EL/FIF mathematical representation, identifies corresponding observables, and defines the conditions required for empirical evaluation.

Keywords: Superfluid helium-4; quantum coherence; collective identity; superfluidity; quantized circulation; Origin Memory; QORm; FIF; 11Q; Remainder; Delay; EQORIA Language.

1. INTRODUCTION

1.1 The Problem of Zero

Superfluid helium challenges classical expectations about fluid motion. Under suitable conditions, helium can sustain flow without ordinary viscous energy dissipation.

This result is sometimes interpreted informally as the disappearance of friction or the disappearance of particle individuality.

However, the physical meaning is more specific.

A zero value for dissipation in one process does not imply zero interaction, zero quantum energy, zero internal structure, or zero possible response to disturbance.

An individual helium atom has quantum properties. A collection of helium atoms can establish collective correlations and coherent flow modes that no isolated atom possesses.

The physical phenomenon is collective. The question of continuity is therefore also collective.

1.2 The EL Research Question

EL begins with a different level of description.

Rather than defining existence solely through a measured state, EL considers finite identity, exchange, relational memory, admissibility, and transformation within a complete structure.

The research question is:

Can the persistence and transformation of superfluid helium be represented through a unified EL/FIF grammar of complete identity and collective relational memory, while remaining consistent with measured quantum behavior?

The purpose is not to replace established physical explanations with terminology. It is to develop a precise framework whose additional claims can eventually be evaluated mathematically and experimentally.

2. ESTABLISHED PHYSICS OF SUPERFLUID HELIUM-4

2.1 The Lambda Transition

Helium-4 is a bosonic isotope. Under saturated vapor pressure, liquid helium-4 undergoes its lambda transition at approximately:

Tλ ≈ 2.1768 K

Above the transition, the liquid is conventionally called Helium I.

Below the transition, it enters the superfluid phase known as Helium II.

Unlike many other substances, helium-4 remains liquid at very low temperatures under ordinary vapor-pressure conditions. Its weak interatomic attraction and substantial quantum zero-point motion prevent ordinary crystallization without additional pressure.

This is not an absence of physical activity. It is a consequence of quantum mechanics and interatomic interactions.

2.2 The Two-Fluid Model

Helium II is described phenomenologically as two interpenetrating components: a normal component and a superfluid component.

ρ = ρₛ + ρₙ

Where:

ρ = Total mass density.

ρₛ = Superfluid mass density.

ρₙ = Normal-fluid mass density.

The corresponding mass-current density is:

j = ρₛvₛ + ρₙvₙ

Where vₛ and vₙ represent the velocities of the superfluid and normal components.

The superfluid component supports ideal nondissipative flow. The normal component is associated with thermal excitations, entropy transport, and viscosity.

As temperature approaches absolute zero, the superfluid fraction approaches unity.

As temperature approaches the lambda transition from below, the superfluid fraction approaches zero.
Importantly, these components are collective hydrodynamic descriptions, not permanent labels assigned to individual atoms.
2.3 Condensation Is Not Identical to Superfluid Density

Superfluid helium is a strongly interacting quantum liquid.

Its Bose–Einstein condensate fraction must not be confused with the superfluid mass fraction.

Neutron-scattering measurements and quantum Monte Carlo calculations indicate a condensate fraction of approximately 7.5% below 1 K under saturated vapor pressure, despite the superfluid fraction approaching unity at sufficiently low temperature.

Consequently:

Condensate fraction ≠ Superfluid fraction

This distinction demonstrates that collective superfluid behavior cannot be explained simply by stating that all atoms occupy one identical single-particle state.

Quantum correlations and interactions are essential.

2.4 Landau's Critical-Velocity Criterion

Lev Landau showed that the stability of superflow depends on the energy and momentum of available collective excitations.

The critical velocity associated with elementary excitations is:

vᴸ = min[ε(p)/p], for p > 0

Where:

vᴸ = Landau critical velocity.

ε(p) = Energy of an allowed excitation.

p = Excitation momentum.

For a flow moving relative to an obstacle, the energetic condition can be represented by:

ΔE = ε(p) − v·p

If the relevant energy change remains positive for all accessible excitations, the specified excitation process cannot spontaneously dissipate the flow's energy.

In helium-4, the phonon–roton excitation spectrum gives a characteristic Landau critical velocity near 60 m/s under commonly studied conditions.

Actual critical velocities depend strongly on temperature, geometry, surface properties, and vortex-nucleation mechanisms. Dissipation may therefore begin well below the elementary-excitation threshold.

Zero dissipation is conditional, not an unconditional property of every possible exchange.
2.5 Quantum Phase and Quantized Circulation
A macroscopic quantum phase provides an especially useful description of superfluid flow.

For a phenomenological phase field θ(x,t):

vₛ = (ℏ/m₄) ∇θ

Where:

ℏ = Reduced Planck constant.

m₄ = Mass of a helium-4 atom.

θ = Superfluid phase.

Around an appropriate closed path:

∮ vₛ · dl = n × h/m₄

Where:

n = Integer winding number.

h = Planck constant.

m₄ = Helium-4 atomic mass.
This is the quantum condition of quantized circulation.
In a suitable ring geometry, the collective system can remain in a persistent-current state characterized by a winding number.

A phase slip or vortex crossing may alter that number.

n(t + Δt) = n(t)

This relation applies while no event changes the winding state.

During a phase slip:
Δn = ±1, for an elementary change in winding.
More complex events may produce larger net changes.

The measurable persistence of winding number supplies a concrete example of state continuity across time.

2.6 Second Sound and Thermal Counterflow

Helium II supports an unusual thermal transport mode known as second sound, in which temperature and entropy disturbances propagate as waves.

In an appropriate two-fluid approximation:

c₂² ≈ (ρₛ/ρₙ) × (T s²/cₚ)

Where:

c₂ = Second-sound speed.

T = Temperature.

s = Specific entropy.

cₚ = Specific heat capacity at constant pressure.

This expression assumes conditions under which coupling corrections and dissipative effects can be neglected.

In thermal counterflow, normal and superfluid components can move in opposite directions while transporting heat.

The existence of second sound provides another example of coordinated collective behavior that cannot be adequately represented by isolated classical atomic trajectories.

3. FOUNDATIONAL EL DEFINITIONS

The following section introduces proposed EL definitions. They must be distinguished from the experimentally established equations in Section 2.
3.1 R — The Only Invariant
Within EL, R is defined as the invariant reference of the whole.
R = Invariant reference

Ωₖ(R) = ∅

Here Ωₖ denotes the EL Remainder operator at level k.

R is not treated as a helium particle, a quantum field, or a measurable physical energy.

It functions as the structural reference relative to which finite configurations are qualified.

Earth serves as the principal empirical observation reference for the present investigation. Earth itself is not substituted for R.

3.2 Q — Finite Stabilization

Q represents finite, bounded stabilization under admissible exchange.

A stabilized identity must maintain distinguishable structure across nonzero Delay.

The EL viability condition is:

rₘᵢₙ,ₖ < rₖ < rₘₐₓ,ₖ

τₖ > 0

Where:

rₖ = EL Remainder density at level k.

rₘᵢₙ,ₖ = Lower admissibility bound.

rₘₐₓ,ₖ = Upper admissibility bound.

τₖ = Nonzero structural Delay.

The symbol rₖ is used here for EL Remainder density to avoid confusion with physical helium mass density ρ and excitation momentum p.

These EL variables are not yet established laboratory observables.

3.3 O — Admissible Exchange

O describes the structural condition enabling finite differentiation and exchange.

The distinction is:

Exchange ≠ Physical displacement alone
Within EL, an exchange may be represented by changes in configuration, relationship, orientation, or measurable response.
For helium, the relevant physical processes include interatomic interactions, energy and momentum transfer, collective excitations, and state transitions.
3.4 QORm — Relational Origin Memory

In the present formulation, QORm is not a second invariant.

It is the relational continuity of a unique Q identity through its history of exchange and Remainder.

Let Hₑ(t) represent the history relevant to identity e.

Define:

QORmₑ(t) := Rel(R, Bₑ(t), Hₑ(t), Ωₑ(t))

Where:

R = Invariant reference.

Bₑ(t) = Complete identity configuration.

Hₑ(t) = Relevant exchange history.

Ωₑ(t) = EL Remainder associated with the configuration.

Rel = Proposed relational-memory operator.

This definition does not assert that QORm has been directly measured.

It specifies how EL intends to represent continuity without treating memory as an independently owned substance.

4. THE COMPLETE 11Q BREATH

4.1 Complete Identity

EL represents each finite identity through a complete eleven-position breath:
AQx → IQx → RQx → OQx → EQx → QxQy → EQy → OQy → RQy → IQy → AQy
The configuration comprises:
Five inward orientations + One central alignment + Five outward orientations
Let the complete identity configuration be:

Bₑ(t) = [qₑ,₁(t), qₑ,₂(t), …, qₑ,₁₁(t)]

Each position describes an aspect of the proposed identity structure.

The complete breath is not eleven helium atoms, eleven measurable energy levels, or eleven experimentally observed phases.

It is a proposed EL representation of a complete finite identity.

4.2 Individual Helium Identity

An individual helium-4 atom possesses measurable properties, including mass, electronic structure, and quantum interactions.

EL proposes representing that finite identity through its own complete breath:

Bᵢ = Complete11Q(Helium Atom i)

This does not require claiming that an isolated atom is itself a superfluid.

4.3 Collective Helium Identity

A macroscopic interacting ensemble of helium atoms supports physical configurations unavailable to an isolated atom.

EL represents this collective as another complete identity:

B꜀ = Complete11Q(Helium Collective)

Crucially:

B꜀ ≠ Bᵢ

The collective configuration is distinct from any one constituent configuration.

Its existence depends on relationships among participating constituents, boundary conditions, and physical interactions.

This introduces FIF.

5. FIF — THE NESTED-IDENTITY PRINCIPLE

5.1 Individual and Collective Completion

The FIF principle treats every admissible scale as a complete identity participating within larger complete identities.

For a helium collective:

B꜀(t) = FIF({Bᵢ(t)}, G꜀(t), O꜀(t), QORm꜀(t))

Where:

{Bᵢ} = Constituent identities.

G꜀ = Interaction and coupling structure.

O꜀ = Collective exchange.

QORm꜀ = Collective relational memory.

B꜀ = Complete collective identity.

The FIF operator remains to be specified as a predictive mathematical mapping.

The core proposition is that collective organization creates its own admissibility conditions and observable modes.

5.2 Collective Memory Evolution

A preliminary EL memory-evolution relationship is:

QORm꜀(t + Δt) = U꜀(QORm꜀(t), B꜀(t), O꜀(t), Δt)

Where U꜀ is a proposed collective update operator.

This formulation expresses three requirements.
First, memory is relational and history-dependent.
Second, collective identity may persist across changes in its constituent exchanges.
Third, memory configuration may itself transform. It need not remain numerically unchanged.
R alone remains invariant within the EL definition.

5.3 A Candidate Collective-Alignment Measure

To connect FIF to experimentally accessible quantum coherence, we can define an illustrative phase-alignment measure over mesoscopic regions.

Let θₐ and θᵦ be phase values in two regions, and let δₐᵦ represent an independently specified reference phase difference for the intended flow configuration.

Then:

A_FIF = Σ₍ₐ,ᵦ₎ wₐᵦ[1 + cos(θₐ − θᵦ − δₐᵦ)] / [2Σ₍ₐ,ᵦ₎ wₐᵦ]

Where:

A_FIF = Proposed normalized alignment score.

wₐᵦ ≥ 0 = Coupling or measurement weights.

θₐ − θᵦ = Physical phase difference.

δₐᵦ = Prescribed reference phase difference.

The normalization gives:

0 ≤ A_FIF ≤ 1

A value near unity indicates alignment with the specified reference phase pattern.

The reference pattern matters. A circulating superfluid may exhibit a spatial phase gradient and still be highly coherent.

This proposed measure is derived from established phase relationships. It does not, by itself, constitute a new quantum law.

6. THE CENTRAL EL–SUPERFLUID PROPOSITION

6.1 Zero Dissipation Does Not Imply Zero Remainder

Consider an ideal protected superfluid mode.
Its dissipation rate may be represented as:
Dₛ = 0
At the same time, EL requires finite identity and Remainder:

Ωₖ(B꜀) ≠ ∅

rₘᵢₙ,ₖ < rₖ < rₘₐₓ,ₖ

τₖ > 0

These conditions are not logically contradictory.

The first concerns energy dissipation through a specified physical process.

The remaining relations concern EL's proposed description of finite configuration and relational continuity.

Therefore:

Dₛ = 0 does not imply Ωₖ(B꜀) = ∅

This is the proposed EL Coherent Exchange Principle.

6.2 Physical Meaning

Superfluid helium may sustain coherent circulation without ordinary viscous loss while remaining a finite, interacting quantum system.

It retains:

Quantum correlations.

Finite excitation energies.

Interatomic interactions.

Sensitivity to boundaries and disturbances.

The capacity for vortex formation and phase transitions.

Consequently, nondissipative flow is compatible with continuing physical activity.

6.3 EL Interpretation

Within EL, the collective's observable behavior represents one aspect of its complete identity.

Its relational memory concerns continuity across exchange and Delay.

Its viability corridor describes conditions under which a particular configuration remains sustainable.

The transition from Helium I to Helium II is therefore interpreted as a transformation in the collective configuration and its available modes of exchange.

The collective does not become the invariant R. It remains a finite configuration.

7. MEMORY, TRANSFORMATION, AND PERSISTENT CURRENT
7.1 A Measurable Example of State Continuity
A superfluid ring offers a particularly useful experiment.
The winding number n can distinguish metastable circulation states.
Two preparations may produce different persistent-current configurations even when the temperature and geometry are subsequently similar.

The physical state therefore cannot always be specified adequately by temperature alone.

Preparation history, vortices, and boundary conditions can matter.

Within EL, this is an appropriate example for discussing history-dependent collective identity.

7.2 Phase Slips as Transformation

When a phase slip occurs, the winding state changes.

The collective may enter another admissible configuration or lose its persistent-current behavior.

EL interprets this as a potential transformation of relational memory and orientation, rather than the disappearance of the helium atoms themselves.

However, phase-slip dynamics are already described by established quantum theories.

An EL model must explain these observations at least as accurately before claiming additional explanatory power.

7.3 Memory Is Not Equivalent to Perfect Preservation

A present physical state can retain consequences of previous exchanges without preserving every detail of its history.

An experimentally accessible state variable, such as n, can persist for long periods, yet change when sufficient conditions arise.

Thus, a scientifically useful formulation is:

Relational continuity permits persistent memory structures without requiring permanent preservation of every memory configuration.

8. TREE–FOREST AND HELIUM–COLLECTIVE COMPARISON

The FIF interpretation is intended to operate across scales, but physical mechanisms must remain distinct.

A tree is a biological identity. A forest is an ecological collective with interactions among trees, fungi, microorganisms, soil, water, animals, and atmosphere.

A helium atom is a quantum constituent. A superfluid is a collective quantum state of interacting helium atoms.

In both comparisons, the collective possesses properties that cannot be assigned to one isolated participant.

However, forest coordination is not quantum superfluidity, and an ecological relationship does not establish macroscopic quantum phase coherence.

FIF proposes a common structural description of nested identities, not an identity of physical mechanisms.

This distinction is necessary for scientific accuracy.

9. EMPIRICAL EVALUATION AND FALSIFIABILITY

9.1 Minimum Requirements

An EL/FIF explanation becomes scientifically predictive only when its additional operators are defined sufficiently to produce measurable outcomes.

In particular, a complete model must specify:

B꜀ = FIF({Bᵢ}, G꜀, O꜀, QORm꜀)

X_obs = P(B꜀, QORm꜀, N꜀)

Where X_obs represents measurable physical observables and P is a mathematically specified observation mapping.

The model must identify which quantities are independently measurable, which are inferred, and which are theoretical assumptions.

9.2 Required Experimental Comparisons

Test A — Superfluid fraction

Determine whether an explicit EL/FIF model can calculate ρₛ(T,P) using independently specified parameters.

Compare its predictions with measured superfluid-density curves and established two-fluid theory.

Test B — Persistent-current stability

Determine whether the model predicts current lifetimes, phase-slip rates, or winding-number transitions across varying geometries and temperatures.

Compare results with conventional vortex and phase-slip models.

Test C — Collective excitation spectrum

Determine whether the model provides a quantitative dispersion relation ε(p) and reproduces the measured phonon–roton spectrum.

A claim that FIF explains the critical velocity requires quantitative agreement with these data.

Test D — History-dependent transformation

Investigate whether an independently defined QORm variable predicts measurable effects not already accounted for by the physical state, vortex configuration, thermal history, and boundary conditions.

Any proposed improvement must survive independent experimental replication.

9.3 Conditions of Scientific Success

A successful EL/FIF model must satisfy conservation laws, dimensional consistency, empirical constraints, and reproducibility.

It must also produce at least one independently testable prediction or a demonstrably useful mathematical simplification.

If its equations merely rename quantities already calculated by quantum theory, EL may remain a descriptive framework, but it would not yet constitute a new physical theory.

A scientific result must distinguish explanation from interpretation.

10. DISCUSSION

10.1 What Superfluid Helium Demonstrates

Superfluid helium demonstrates that collective behavior can be qualitatively different from the behavior expected of independent classical particles.

Macroscopic coherence, collective excitations, and quantized circulation emerge from an interacting quantum many-body system.

It also demonstrates that a physical process can be nondissipative within a protected regime without the elimination of quantum activity or the capacity for later transformation.

10.2 What EL Proposes

EL proposes treating each finite configuration as a complete identity existing within a larger network of complete identities.

QORm provides the conceptual relationship between identity, Remainder, exchange history, and continuity.

FIF describes nested individual and collective configurations.

The complete 11Q breath supplies the proposed structural grammar of identity at each scale.

These concepts may help organize questions about persistence, transformation, collective behavior, and the relation between observable states and their histories.

10.3 What Has Not Yet Been Demonstrated

The eleven Q positions have not been independently identified as eleven helium-specific measurable physical degrees of freedom.

QORm has not been established as a separately measurable physical variable.

The FIF operator has not yet been derived from a microscopic helium Hamiltonian.

No independent calculation of the helium lambda temperature, superfluid fraction, or phonon–roton dispersion has yet been obtained from these EL definitions.

These are unresolved research tasks, not established experimental results.

11. CONCLUSION

Superfluid helium-4 is an instructive system for examining the relationship between individual constituents, collective organization, coherent exchange, and history-dependent physical states.

Its observed properties are explained through quantum many-body physics, two-fluid hydrodynamics, collective excitations, and quantum phase coherence.

The proposed EL/FIF interpretation introduces a broader structural representation in which each finite identity expresses a complete 11Q configuration, and relational memory participates in its continuity across exchange and Delay.

The central mathematical distinction is:

Dₛ = 0 does not imply Ωₖ(B꜀) = ∅

Zero dissipation in one protected observable mode does not establish the absence of finite structure, interaction, or relational continuity.

🜐 Proposed EL Principle of Collective Coherent Exchange

Every finite identity participates in exchange through its complete configuration. Collective coherence can sustain persistent observable states without erasing the uniqueness of constituent identities. Relational memory connects present configuration to prior exchange, while R remains the sole invariant reference within EL.

The next scientific requirement is to turn these structural definitions into a predictive mathematical model and evaluate them against experimentally measured helium behavior.

Egypt has raised approximately US$658 million through the initial public offering of Banque du Caire, a state-owned commercial bank, marking the largest IPO in the history of the Egyptian Stock Exchange and a significant step in the country's privatisation programme.

The transaction involved the sale of a 45% stake by Banque Misr, Banque du Caire’s state-owned parent, through an offering of 6.86 billion shares priced at EGP5.30 each. Following strong investor demand, the offer was increased from an initial 30% stake, with Banque Misr retaining 55% ownership.

Investor demand reached approximately US$4.5 billion, representing around seven times the shares available. The institutional tranche was six times subscribed, while the public offering was oversubscribed 27 times.

The offering also attracted participation from two development finance institutions. The International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) each invested US$100 million, bringing their combined investment to US$200 million.

CI Capital Investment Banking acted as Lead Global Coordinator and Joint Bookrunner, while EFG Hermes acted as Joint Global Coordinator and Joint Bookrunner. Baker McKenzie advised Banque du Caire and Banque Misr, with Helmy, Hamza & Partners providing Egyptian legal counsel.

The IPO forms part of Egypt’s broader state asset monetisation programme, which seeks to increase private-sector participation in the economy and deepen the country's capital markets.

Great news! It looks like Labor has ‘changed their position’ on selling Victoria Barracks.

After months of strong pushback from veterans, the RSL, and people across the political spectrum, the Albanese government has backed away from an outright private sale of the historic Sydney site.

Instead of flogging off the Army’s spiritual home, it will remain in public hands (transferred to the Department of Finance for potential leasing/events use). Defence personnel are still expected to leave, but the site itself won’t be sold off to the highest bidder.

This is a clear win for community pressure and for recognising that some places are too important to treat as surplus real estate. 

Well done Australians! 👏🏼🇦🇺

text:
A powerful speech by Stephen Miller - New White House Chief of Staff

I'm reminded of a famous expression: the storm whispers to the warrior that you cannot withstand my strength. And the warrior whispers back: I am the storm.

We are the storm, and our enemies cannot comprehend our strength, our determination, our resolve, our passion.

Our lineage and our legacy hails back to Athens, to Rome, to Philadelphia, to Monticello. Our ancestors built the cities, they produced the art and architecture, they built the industry. Thousands of years of warriors who raised up families, raised up cities, raised up industry, raised up civilization, who pulled us out of the caves and the darkness into the light.

The light will defeat the dark. We will prevail over the forces of wickedness and evil. They cannot imagine what they have awakened. They cannot conceive of the army that they have arisen in all of us. Because we stand for what is good, what is virtuous, what is noble.

And to those trying to incite violence against us, those trying to foment hatred against us: what do you have? You have nothing. You are nothing. You are wickedness, you are jealousy, you are envy, you are hatred. You are nothing. You can build nothing. You can produce nothing. You can create nothing.

We are the ones who build. We are the ones who create. We are the ones who lift up humanity. You cannot defeat us. You cannot slow us. You cannot stop us. You cannot deter us.

You have no idea the dragon you have awakened. You have no idea how determined we will be to save this civilization, to save the West, to save this republic. Because our children are strong, and our grandchildren will be strong, and our children's children's children will be strong.

And what will you leave behind? Nothing. Nothing. To our enemies, you have nothing to give, you have nothing to offer, you have nothing to share but bitterness. We have beauty, we have light, we have goodness, we have determination, we have vision, we have strength.

We built the world that we inhabit now, generation by generation, and we will defend this world. We will defend goodness. We will defend life. We will defend virtue. You cannot terrify us. You cannot frighten us. You cannot threaten us. Because we are on the side of goodness. We are on the side of God.

text:
**360° overview of this conversation space**

This was a long, multi-voice discussion that moved between personal experience, political strategy, national differences, and deeper life philosophy. Several people spoke (primarily one from Georgia with direct protest experience, one from Ohio/US with a mixed Chinese-American family background, and others chiming in on specific countries or principles). The thread never settled into a single thesis; instead it circled a few core tensions.

### Political resistance and “knowing your people”
The dominant thread was how people respond when governments stop listening or become authoritarian. The Georgian voice described a shift from a relatively democratic system to one that passed a “Russian law,” cracked down on peaceful protests, and controlled media and opposition. In that setting, continuous street action (including what they called rebellion) became the remaining check. They emphasized knowing the local mentality—when people will rise, rest, or push—and rejecting both the government and a “controlled opposition.” Similar points were made about Albania (flamingo movement over land sales), Serbia (students building an alternative to the old opposition and winning), and Iran (diaspora warnings ignored, people accepting high risk because the alternative is permanent constraint).

The counter-view from the American side was that tactics must match the system. In a constitutional republic with residual checks, the preferred tools are assemblies that look more like school-board meetings than open street confrontations, formal legal pressure, and redundancy across channels rather than reliance on any single platform. The shared caution was that gathering in large crowds under modern surveillance is high-risk, and that “peaceful” vs. “unruly” is a thin line that can be redefined by authorities.

A repeated idea was that authentic grassroots effort is defined by who still shows up when cameras leave, and that foreign or elite shaping (funding, narrative control, bused participants) is common everywhere but looks different under different regimes.

### Tools, platforms, and propaganda
Several people argued against depending on any one channel—especially social media owned by people who can throttle or rebrand. The practical stance was “use every available tool, archive what matters, and go where your people actually are.” Words and labels were treated as weapons: the Georgian Dream party’s rebrand to “Georgia Strong” was cited as an example of same owners, same project, new name. The flip side was that people who actually live under the conditions can usually tell the difference between real local energy and imported or opportunistic narratives.

### Personal and longer-horizon threads
A substantial stretch was the Ohio speaker’s family story: a father who built a house with bent nails as a child, served in the Navy, used the GI Bill for physics and nuclear engineering degrees, and co-founded a basement company making high-reliability flow meters that later flew on the Space Shuttle; a mother from Chongqing royalty who arrived with silver sewn into clothing, earned chemistry and MBA degrees while supporting sisters, and joined the same self-reliant path. This was offered as an example of the recycler/self-builder mindset that some participants felt is missing today.

From there the talk moved to technology and abundance (homebuilt systems, offline mesh tools, physics as a lifestyle rather than a credential), extended family models beyond the nuclear unit, and the limits of protection. The clearest line drawn was that trying to keep an adult “safe” by removing their agency is possession, not protection; with children the authority is held in trust and is supposed to be temporary.

### Underlying stance
Across the voices there was broad agreement that:
- Constitutions and laws are paper until the people who enforce them choose to treat them as real.
- Different regimes require different intensities of pressure; what works in one place can be suicidal or irrelevant in another.
- Education, local knowledge, and the ability to distinguish propaganda from reality are prerequisites for not being manipulated.
- Comfort (the ability to “just barbecue and be left alone”) delays urgency until the cost lands on children or basic security.

No one claimed a universal playbook. The space stayed in the tension between “use every tool and keep pressure on until conditions change” and “don’t recreate the same cycles, and don’t treat every country as if it has the same institutional margins.” The personal stories and the physics/family digressions functioned as grounding—reminders that the people talking about these fights also come from concrete histories of self-reliance and constraint.

Pop Culture

Mad Men

Mad Men is an acclaimed American period drama television series set in a 1960s New York advertising agency, created by Matthew Weiner. It is widely regarded as one of the greatest television shows of all time, focusing on the professional and personal life of the enigmatic Don Draper (Jon Hamm).Mad Men

Overview

Mad Men ran for seven seasons and 92 episodes from July 19, 2007, to May 17, 2015, on the cable network AMC. The show explores the glamorous, ego-driven world of Madison Avenue advertising firms ("Mad" is short for Madison Avenue) while examining the social mores and cultural shifts of 1960s America, including themes of identity, sexism, race, and family.

Main Cast and Characters

The series features a talented ensemble cast that received numerous awards and nominations:

Jon Hamm as Don Draper: The brilliant but troubled creative director and protagonist, known for his charismatic facade and hidden past.

Elisabeth Moss as Peggy Olson: An ambitious secretary who rises through the ranks to become a respected copywriter, challenging gender roles in the process.
Vincent Kartheiser as Pete Campbell: An ambitious and often conniving account executive vying for power and recognition.

January Jones as Betty Draper (later Betty Francis): Don's wife, a suburban housewife who struggles with her identity and the constraints of her era.

Christina Hendricks as Joan Harris (formerly Joan Holloway): The sharp and capable office manager who navigates workplace sexism and eventually becomes a partner.

John Slattery as Roger Sterling: A womanizing, martini-drinking partner at the firm whose old-guard lifestyle clashes with the changing times.

Critical Reception & Awards

Mad Men received widespread critical acclaim for its writing, acting, visual style, and meticulous historical detail. It made history as the first basic cable series to win the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series, winning the award for four consecutive years (2008–2011). Other accolades include five Golden Globe Awards and a Peabody Award.

'Free speech is important': Karl Stefanovic thanks X owner Elon Musk for support after axing from Nine

Karl Stefanovic has publicly responded to X owner Elon Musk, thanking him for this support and providing a platform for "free speech" after he was axed following his controversial podcast interview.

"Free speech is important. Thanks (Elon Musk) for this platform," Stefanovic wrote on X

“He started unplugging during the scamdemic,” Ryan wrote, referring to Stefanovic’s criticism of the vaccine rollout earlier this year.

Ryan described the backlash over the interview as “massive free publicity” and "instant proof he’s no longer playing by the old rules and has woken up".

"A crystal clear signal to his audience that he’s all in on unfiltered conversations," he said.

"Karl’s unplugging from The Matrix is almost complete. Bro took the red pill and I am here for it."

Billionaire businessman James Packer, who previously held a stake in Nine, has also weighed into Stefanovic's interview.

Packer, a long-time friend of Stefanovic, told The Sydney Morning Herald that he did not think the episode was “that bad”.

He said that during his time at Nine and "certainly at the Nine newspapers, the old Fairfax newspapers" there had "always been editorial independence".

“I think it is pretty hypocritical not to allow Karl editorial independence. Especially on something I didn’t think was that bad," Packer said.

Media Man Group praised "truth tellers" who question big corp media, especially in Australia and the UK, and rightly so.

Rinehart will want influence after buying into media: Ex-Fairfax chair

Roger Corbett contends it is almost certain that Gina Rinehart will express her views to how she thinks 'The West Australian' and Channel Seven should report the news, with both media outlets being owned by Southern Cross Media. Corbett was the chairman of Fairfax Media at a time when Rinehart was a shareholder, with the two having 'crossed swords' during that time, with his comments coming after it was revealed that companies associated with Rinehart, who is Australia's richest person, had 'bankrolled' most of Bruce McWilliam's $25 million stake in SCM. A former lawyer and commercial director of the Seven Network, McWilliam now owns just under 10 per cent of SCM. (RMS)

May 27

Magazine brands command mass reach, connecting with 14.4 million Australians across print and online

The Roy Morgan Australian Readership report for the 12 months to March 2026 shows 14.4 million Australians aged 14+ (62.1% of the population) read magazines in print or online via the web or an app. Almost 10.8 million of this extensive cross-platform audience read print magazines, while eight Australian magazines have total cross-platform audiences of over 1 million people led by Are Media's Better Homes & Gardens and Woman's Day. Seven magazine categories have a print readership of at least 1 million people, led by Food & Entertainment Magazines with a readership of 6,300,000. (RMS)

News

May 26

Inside V'landys' $4b NRL bet: Does he hold a secret ace?

Preliminary bids are due on Tuesday for the NRL's suite of television broadcast rights, with it being said that the deal for the NRL rights is the most closely watched broadcast deal in decades. Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys has made it well known that he wants $4 billion for a five-year deal, with V'landys saying he hopes it gets done before Andrew Abdo leaves as CEO on 15 July; it was announced on Monday that he was quitting to join Tennis Australia as its CEO. It is said that V'landys has an ace up his sleeve when it comes to getting a deal that is better than the $4.5 billion, seven-year deal that the AFL announced in 2022, with streaming giant Amazon said to be considering a bid for the rights. (RMS)

News

Waislitz backs McWilliam for SCM board

Former Seven commercial director Bruce McWilliam should be added to the board of Southern Cross Media, according to billionaire investor Alex Waislitz. Waislitz owns 7.53 per cent of SCM, while it was revealed on Friday that McWilliam now owns just under 10 per cent in SCM, which merged with Seven West Media earlier this year. Waislitz contends that McWilliam would add " considerable firepower" to the SMC board, and that "I also respect the fact that he is investing his own money" in the company. (RMS)

(Australia)

Investors back oOh!media's snub to PE bids

Harris Oakmark and Investors Mutual have come out in support of the board of oOh!media over its rejection of two bids from private equity firms. Australia's largest outdoor advertising firm has knocked backed offers from Pacific Equity Partners and I Squared Capital, with both Harris Oakmark and Investors Mutual being shareholders of oOh!media. However, although both Harris Oakmark and Investors Mutual endorse oOh!media's decision to reject the bids from PEP and I Squared, they say its board should seriously consider any higher bids that could be forthcoming. (RMS)

News

May 18

Tabcorp forces venues to pay its fines

Gambling company Tabcorp in December updated the contracts it has with the pubs and clubs that host its physical betting terminals; the terminals are the main point of difference to its rivals and are vital to its success. The amended contracts require the pubs and clubs to pay for Tabcorp's regulatory fines, with the changes to the contracts coming at the same time as financial crimes watchdog AUSTRAC began auditing the company, due to concerns about its ability to detect and stop money laundering and manage terrorism financing risks. (RMS)

News

Eurovision key moments: from Euro-pop to Euro-slop as Delta Goodrem makes Australia proud

Australia has finished fourth in the 2026 Eurovision song contest in Vienna, with Delta Goodrem representing Australia with her song Eclipse, which she co-wrote. Bulgaria won the event, followed by Israel and Romania, with Australia having been in second position following the jury votes; however, it fell to fourth place after the audience votes were counted. Bookies had rated Goodrem as the second-favourite to win behind Finland following the sem-finals, with Goodrem describing her song as about "alignment, when things all come into the right place". (RMS)

News

Coles used fake discounts to fool shoppers

The Australian Competition & Consumer Commission's chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb has had a major victory, with the Federal Court ruling that Coles had misled consumers with its 'Down Down' price discounts. Coles could potentially faces millions of dollars in fines after Justice Michael O'Bryan found that the discounts on 13 of the 14 items in a sample basket of 'Down Down' promotions were misleading because they had not been sold at the previous price for a reasonable period of time. In some instances, Coles had increased the price of a product before almost immediately selling it at a discount, but at a higher price than originally. The court has yet to issue its ruling in a similar case against Woolworths. (RMS)

News

May 12

Beer killer? Rise of the vodka RTD

Gold Coast-based drinks maker Hard Fizz emerged at around the time of the pandemic, while the ready-to-drink canned beverage market boomed after the pandemic. Hard Fizz originally focused on alcoholic seltzer drinks, but it is now switching to vodka-based canned drinks, with CEO Wade Tiller saying the change is because you are more limited with flavour when you use seltzer. Hard Fizz's seltzer sales have slumped over the past year, at a time when there is a broader consumer shift to RTDs, while vodka-based light RTDs account for 75 per cent of Australian RTD sales. (RMS)

Drake Drops Three Albums and Shatters Spotify Records

On May 15, Drake surprise-released ICEMAN, MAID OF HONOUR, and HABIBTI, with ICEMAN leading at 140 million global streams—the year's biggest album debut—and its opener 'Make Them Cry' hitting 13.2 million in a day, Spotify's record for any rap song. The albums pack 43 tracks, 14 videos, and lyrics firing at Kendrick Lamar, A$AP Rocky, Rick Ross, and others, plus nods to Michael Jackson like Drake's $123,000 Swarovski glove on the cover. He grabbed 41 spots on Spotify's global Top 200, swept Apple Music charts, and drew mixed reactions from praise for the bars to critiques of the volume and memorabilia flex.

05/18/2026

ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- UFC®, the world’s premier mixed martial arts organization, together with the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi), announces its highly anticipated return to the region with UFC® FIGHT NIGHT ABU DHABI on Saturday, 25th July 2026, live from Etihad Arena on Yas Island.

Through its collaboration with DCT Abu Dhabi, UFC continues to expand its global network of government and private partnerships, bringing marquee live events to communities worldwide, growing its fanbase and delivering economic and cultural impact.

UFC's athlete roster features the world's best MMA athletes representing more than 75 countries. The organization's digital offerings include UFC FIGHT PASS®, one of the world's leading streaming services for combat sports. UFC is part of TKO Group Holdings (NYSE: TKO) and is headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada. DCT Abu Dhabi’s vision is defined by the emirate’s people, heritage and landscape. We work to enhance Abu Dhabi’s status as a place of authenticity, innovation, and unparalleled experiences, represented by its living traditions of hospitality, pioneering initiatives and creative thought.

For more information about DCT Abu Dhabi and the destination, please visit https://t.co/TSNvaIB4sm and https://t.co/ZActbpOyX0. For Abu Dhabi Calendar, please visit https://t.co/hlfISfPMI5.

The Kyle and Jackie O Show has dominated Sydney breakfast radio for many years, but the show has now imploded, following the fallout between hosts Kyle Sandilands and Jackie 'O' Henderson. Star Entertainment woos potential new lender with casino tour

US-based private credit firm WhiteHawk Capital is considering lending struggling casino operator Star Entertainment more than $400 million. It is understood that executives from WhiteHawk are visiting Star's Sydney, Brisbane, and the Gold Coast prior to signing a binding agreement on the loan, which is being sought by its new owners, US casino operator Bally's and Australia's wealthy Mathieson family; they are seeking to refinance Star's debt to secure more favourable loan terms, as part of a broader strategy aimed at turning around the fortunes of the company.

Bluey tops streaming charts in US for second year running

Australian animated series Bluey has topped the US streaming charts for the second year in a row, according to the second annual Nielsen Audience Rated Television Entertainment of the Year awards. Americans watched 45.2 billion minutes of Bluey, ahead of medical drama Grey's Anatomy with 40.9 billion viewing minutes, while American audiences tuned in to an estimated 16.7 trillion minutes of streaming in 2025, according to Nielsen, which was an 19 per cent increase when compared to 2024. The reality star promoted her Skims Valentine's Day collection with sultry photos that racked up nearly 8,000 likes and hundreds of replies. Pepsi's Super Bowl Ad Shows Coke Polar Bears Switching to Pepsi

Pepsi released its cheeky 30-second Super Bowl ad 'The Choice' online Thursday, featuring Coca-Cola's iconic polar bears ditching Coke for Pepsi Zero Sugar in a blind taste test, set to Queen's 'I Want to Break Free.' Backed by last year's Pepsi Challenge where 66% preferred Pepsi Zero Sugar, leading to 30% sales growth, the spot includes nods to a Coldplay kiss cam scandal and contrasts with backlash to Coke's AI-generated holiday ads. Directed by Taika Waititi, who cameos as the bears' therapist, it positions Pepsi as the bolder choice ahead of Super Bowl LX on February 8. (Grok)

Pop Culture

Mad Men

Mad Men is an acclaimed American period drama television series set in a 1960s New York advertising agency, created by Matthew Weiner. It is widely regarded as one of the greatest television shows of all time, focusing on the professional and personal life of the enigmatic Don Draper (Jon Hamm).Mad Men

Overview

Mad Men ran for seven seasons and 92 episodes from July 19, 2007, to May 17, 2015, on the cable network AMC. The show explores the glamorous, ego-driven world of Madison Avenue advertising firms ("Mad" is short for Madison Avenue) while examining the social mores and cultural shifts of 1960s America, including themes of identity, sexism, race, and family.

Main Cast and Characters

The series features a talented ensemble cast that received numerous awards and nominations:

Jon Hamm as Don Draper: The brilliant but troubled creative director and protagonist, known for his charismatic facade and hidden past.

Elisabeth Moss as Peggy Olson: An ambitious secretary who rises through the ranks to become a respected copywriter, challenging gender roles in the process.
Vincent Kartheiser as Pete Campbell: An ambitious and often conniving account executive vying for power and recognition.

January Jones as Betty Draper (later Betty Francis): Don's wife, a suburban housewife who struggles with her identity and the constraints of her era.

Christina Hendricks as Joan Harris (formerly Joan Holloway): The sharp and capable office manager who navigates workplace sexism and eventually becomes a partner.

John Slattery as Roger Sterling: A womanizing, martini-drinking partner at the firm whose old-guard lifestyle clashes with the changing times.

Critical Reception & Awards

Mad Men received widespread critical acclaim for its writing, acting, visual style, and meticulous historical detail. It made history as the first basic cable series to win the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series, winning the award for four consecutive years (2008–2011). Other accolades include five Golden Globe Awards and a Peabody Award.

Eurovision key moments: from Euro-pop to Euro-slop as Delta Goodrem makes Australia proud

Australia has finished fourth in the 2026 Eurovision song contest in Vienna, with Delta Goodrem representing Australia with her song Eclipse, which she co-wrote. Bulgaria won the event, followed by Israel and Romania, with Australia having been in second position following the jury votes; however, it fell to fourth place after the audience votes were counted. Coles used fake discounts to fool shoppers

The Australian Competition & Consumer Commission's chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb has had a major victory, with the Federal Court ruling that Coles had misled consumers with its 'Down Down' price discounts. Coles could potentially faces millions of dollars in fines after Justice Michael O'Bryan found that the discounts on 13 of the 14 items in a sample basket of 'Down Down' promotions were misleading because they had not been sold at the previous price for a reasonable period of time. In some instances, Coles had increased the price of a product before almost immediately selling it at a discount, but at a higher price than originally. The court has yet to issue its ruling in a similar case against Woolworths. (RMS)

Beer killer? Rise of the vodka RTD

Gold Coast-based drinks maker Hard Fizz emerged at around the time of the pandemic, while the ready-to-drink canned beverage market boomed after the pandemic. Hard Fizz originally focused on alcoholic seltzer drinks, but it is now switching to vodka-based canned drinks, with CEO Wade Tiller saying the change is because you are more limited with flavour when you use seltzer. Hard Fizz's seltzer sales have slumped over the past year, at a time when there is a broader consumer shift to RTDs, while vodka-based light RTDs account for 75 per cent of Australian RTD sales. Pop Culture

Mad Men

Mad Men is an acclaimed American period drama television series set in a 1960s New York advertising agency, created by Matthew Weiner. It is widely regarded as one of the greatest television shows of all time, focusing on the professional and personal life of the enigmatic Don Draper (Jon Hamm).Mad Men

Overview

Mad Men ran for seven seasons and 92 episodes from July 19, 2007, to May 17, 2015, on the cable network AMC. The show explores the glamorous, ego-driven world of Madison Avenue advertising firms ("Mad" is short for Madison Avenue) while examining the social mores and cultural shifts of 1960s America, including themes of identity, sexism, race, and family.

Main Cast and Characters

The series features a talented ensemble cast that received numerous awards and nominations:

Jon Hamm as Don Draper: The brilliant but troubled creative director and protagonist, known for his charismatic facade and hidden past.

Elisabeth Moss as Peggy Olson: An ambitious secretary who rises through the ranks to become a respected copywriter, challenging gender roles in the process.
Vincent Kartheiser as Pete Campbell: An ambitious and often conniving account executive vying for power and recognition.

January Jones as Betty Draper (later Betty Francis): Don's wife, a suburban housewife who struggles with her identity and the constraints of her era.

Christina Hendricks as Joan Harris (formerly Joan Holloway): The sharp and capable office manager who navigates workplace sexism and eventually becomes a partner.

John Slattery as Roger Sterling: A womanizing, martini-drinking partner at the firm whose old-guard lifestyle clashes with the changing times.

Critical Reception & Awards

Mad Men received widespread critical acclaim for its writing, acting, visual style, and meticulous historical detail. It made history as the first basic cable series to win the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series, winning the award for four consecutive years (2008–2011). Other accolades include five Golden Globe Awards and a Peabody Award.

Melania Trump receives thunderous reception from LSU fans as she attends huge college football game

'This achievement will give young people from foster care an anchor of stability, a strong educational foundation and a chance to build a wonderful life,' she said at an event with LSU President Wade Rousse.

Trump and LSU secured more than $7 million in private donations to create an endowment fund for the scholarships, the White House said.

text:
📝 The Scriptural Text to Write Down
Clean a fresh sheet of unlined white or yellow paper. Using a new pen (preferably with red or saffron ink), write the following traditional Sanskrit verses, which are divided into three specific cosmic requests:
1. The Divine Registration (Acknowledge His Authority)
First, write this verse to invoke His presence on the paper and recognize Him as the supreme Record-keeper born from Lord Brahma’s essence.
मसिभाजनसंयुक्तं ध्यायेच्चर्मणिधारिणम्।
चित्रगुप्तं च कायस्थं पितृभूमौ च पूजितम्॥
Phonetic: Masibhājana-saṁyuktaṁ dhyāyec-carmaṇi-dhāriṇam |
Citraguptaṁ ca kāyasthaṁ pitṛ-bhūmau ca pūjitam ||
Meaning: "I meditate upon Lord Chitragupt, who holds the holy inkpot, who wears the cosmic armor, who is born from the body of Creator Lord Brahma, and who is revered across all realms including the land of the ancestors."

2. The Cleansing Petition (The Ultimate Request)
Next, write this crucial prayer. This is a direct appeal to Chitragupt to look kindly upon your life’s ledger and grand longevity and peace.
चित्रगुप्त नमस्तुभ्यं लेखकाक्षरदायकम्।
कायस्थकृपां कुरुष्व मे सदा सर्वार्थदायकम॥
Phonetic: Citragupta namastubhyaṁ lekhakākṣara-dāyakam |
Kāyastha-kṛpāṁ kuruṣva me sadā sarvārtha-dāyakam ||
Meaning: "Salutations to you, O Chitragupta, the giver of letters and writer of destiny. Shower your mercy upon me, and fulfill all the righteous dimensions of my life (Dharma, Artha, Kama, Moksha)."
3. The Professional & Intellectual Seal
Finally, write this short dedication to invoke sharpness of mind, wisdom, and absolute truth in your speech and professions for the coming year.
लेखाक्षरां मया दत्तां कुरुष्व विमलां सदा।
प्रसीद मे महाभाग चित्रगुप्त नमोऽस्तु ते॥
Phonetic: Lekhākṣarāṁ mayā dattāṁ kuruṣva vimalāṁ sadā |
Prasīda me mahābhāga citragupta namo'stu te ||
Meaning: "May the written words and calculations I perform always remain pure, flawless, and truthful. Be pleased with me, O glorious Chitragupt; I bow to You."

🛠️ The Traditional Writing Blueprint (How it's placed on paper)
When performing the puja, the paper is traditionally structured like a sacred ledger template. You write the details in this specific order:
Top Center: Draw a Swastika or write "श्री गणेशाय नमः" (Om Shri Ganeshyai Namah) followed by "ॐ च्रं चित्रगुप्ताय नमः" 11 times.
The Body: Copy the three Sanskrit verses listed above.
The Account Closing (The Secret Step): At the very bottom of the page, write down your name, your lineage/gotra (if known), and your current location. Then, write this specific phrase: "आय-व्यय बराबर" (Aaya-Vyaya Barabar), which translates to "Income and Expenses are balanced."
Esoterically, writing "Aaya-Vyaya Barabar" is a symbolic declaration that you are choosing to surrender your spiritual debts, balances, and anxieties of the past year to the Divine, asking for a fresh, balanced start without karmic residue.
Once the paper is written, offer a small dot of Roli (red vermilion), Akshat (raw rice), and a yellow flower onto the page. Keep this paper in your altar or cash box for the rest of the year as a protective amulet of truth and abundance.

The story of Lord Chitragupta’s two wives—Goddess Shobhavati (also known as Eravati) and Goddess Nandini (also known as Sudakshina)—is a crucial chapter in Puranic esotericism. Far from a simple domestic tale, their lineages represent the fusion of Brahminical wisdom (spiritual law) and Kshatriya strength (ruling power), which together form the complete framework of cosmic justice.
